The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Collection means, where a person who, under agreements, verbal or written, with or without compensation, does the work of collecting and/or transporting solid waste from industries, offices, retail outlets, businesses, institutions, and/or similar locations, or from residential dwellings; provided that this definition shall not include an individual collecting and/or transporting waste from his own single-family dwelling unit.
Commercial premises means all premises not residential as residential is hereinafter defined in this section. Where the classification of a commercial premises cannot be determined conclusively from the foregoing definitions, such determination shall be at the discretion of the mayor or his designated representative. It is the intention of the mayor and council that any such unclassified commercial premises shall be placed in a class commensurate with the volume of solid waste produced by said premises.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where any treatment, utilization, processing, or deposition of solid waste occurs.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal, including administration, personnel, land, equipment, design, and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Disposal site means the location of land area where the final deposition of solid waste occurs.
Garbage means putrescible animal and vegetable wastes resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking, and consumption of food.
Hazardous waste means solid or liquid waste material resulting from the manufacture or use of pesticides and drugs (other than normal household use); pathological wastes; highly flammable or explosive wastes; toxic wastes; sewage sludges; and other waste material determined to be a likely hazard to the public health, safety, or environment, except radioactive waste materials as provided for in Rules of the Department of Human Resources, chapter 270-5-20, entitled Radioactive Materials.
Industrial waste means waste materials generated in industrial operations.
Open dump means a disposal site at which solid waste from one or more sources is consolidated and left to decompose, burn, or to otherwise create environmental pollution or nuisance.
Putrescible wastes means wastes that are capable of being decomposed by microorganisms, including kitchen wastes, manure, offal, hatchery and poultry wastes, and garbage.
Reclamation means a controlled method of sorting and storing solid wastes for future use in accordance with an approved plan.
Refuse means all putrescible and nonputrescible solid wastes (except body wastes), including garbage, rubbish, ashes, street cleanings, dead animals, abandoned automobiles, and solid commercial and industrial wastes.
Residential premises means all residential dwellings except motels and other dwellings offering lodging for hire.
Rubbish means nonputrescible solid wastes (excluding ashes), consisting of both combustible and noncombustible wastes, such as paper, cardboard, tin cans, wood, glass, bedding, crockery and similar materials.
Sanitary land filling means a method of disposing of putrescible waste and/or hazardous waste on land by placing an earth cover thereon.
Scavenge means uncontrolled picking from discarded waste materials.
Solid waste means putrescible and nonputrescible wastes (except water-carried body wastes) including garbage, rubbish, ashes, street refuse, dead animals, sewage sludges, animal manures, industrial wastes, residue from incineration, food-processing wastes, construction wastes, hazardous wastes, and any other waste material in a solid or semisolid state not otherwise defined in this chapter.
Solid waste handling means the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposing of solid wastes, or any combination thereof.
Transfer station means a facility used to transfer solid wastes from one transportation vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal facility.

(a) Generally. No person shall keep or store solid waste outside of any residence or building within the city, except in proper containers for collection or otherwise prepared, as set forth herein or under the express prior approval of the superintendent of public works. Any unauthorized accumulation of solid waste is hereby declared to be a nuisance and is prohibited. The superintendent of public works by written notice shall notify the owner or occupant of any premises with such solid waste accumulation to remove same. Failure to remove such accumulation within two weeks of the date of such written notice to do so shall be deemed a violation of these regulations and subject to penalties hereinafter set forth. A separate violation shall be deemed committed each day during or upon which such unlawful accumulation continues.
(b) Containers.
(1) Garbage containers shall be provided by the owner or occupant of each residence or establishment sufficient in number to accommodate such waste generated by the residence or establishment between collections. Containers shall be of durable metal or plastic, watertight, nonabsorbent, rust-resistant, rodentproof, and easily cleanable. They shall be equipped with handles and tightly fitted covers and shall have a capacity of not less than 15 gallons nor more than 55 gallons, except that bulk containers of a type accepted by the superintendent of public works as suitable for mechanical collection services or by publicly owned equipment used for such collection may be used. Containers failing to comply with these provisions or which have defects causing them to scatter waste upon the ground during collection or causing them to hamper or injure the persons collecting waste shall be promptly replaced.
(2) Disposable paper or plastic bags of a type, size, and material designed for solid waste disposal may be used to contain refuse for storage and collection, provided they are unbroken, sealed, and loaded in such manner that normal handling will not cause the bag to open.
(3) No person shall place any solid waste in any container not owned by that person or in any container whose owner has not given said person permission to deposit solid waste in such container. No person shall place any solid waste in any container owned by the city without express permission of the city.
(c) Rubbish. Rubbish may be stored for collection in paper-board boxes or other throwaway containers strong enough to retain the waste; loose paper or cuttings shall be tied in bundles. Rubbish containers or bundles shall not exceed 50 pounds in weight. Rubbish containers or bundles shall be placed for collection beside the solid waste containers.
(d) Placement. On days designated as collection days for the respective routes by the superintendent of public works, garbage and/or rubbish shall be placed for collection on the curb or beside the roadway in front of the residence or establishment owning same, or if the property abuts on an alley, at the rear of the property, but not in the gutter or in the street or alley in such manner as to interfere with pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(e) Scavenging. No person other than the owner or authorized collection personnel shall sift the contents of or remove anything from containers, boxes, or bundles containing garbage or rubbish.

Local civic group means local—primarily serving the needs of a particular limited district; civic group—of or relating to a citizen, a city, citizenship, or community affairs.

1150:
(a) Permits required. It shall be unlawful for any person, group, organization, association, club or other entity to conduct or cause to be conducted any special event in the city without first obtaining from the city a valid permit for such special event.
(b) Geographic limitations. Each special event shall be conducted, located and limited to the specific geographic area authorized and permitted under the terms, conditions and restrictions of the city permit issued for each such special event and in accordance with the provisions of this division.
(c) Time limitations. Each special event shall be limited in time to the dates and time periods authorized and permitted under the terms, conditions and restrictions of the city permit issued for each such special event and in accordance with the provisions of this division.
(d) Activity limitations. Each special event shall be limited to those activities authorized and permitted under the terms, conditions and restrictions of the city permit issued for each such special event and in accordance with the provisions of this division.
(e) Application. A producer of a special event shall make application for such permit at city hall in a form prescribed by the city, and file such completed application with the city clerk. Such applications may be obtained form the office of the city clerk.
(f) Application fee. A nonrefundable application fee as provided in the city fee schedule shall be paid upon the filing of each special event application with the city clerk.
(g) Time requirements for filing. Applications for special events which request the use of any public property, street, sidewalk or right-of-way within the city, or for events which are to occur on private property and impact government services on a public property, street, sidewalk or right-of-way, and which propose more than six persons as attendees, shall be filed with the city clerk at least 60 days prior to the date the special event is scheduled to occur. Applications for such special events the use or for events which are to occur on private property and impact government services on a public property, street, sidewalk or right-of-way, and which propose six or fewer persons as attendees, shall be filed with the city clerk at least 30 days prior to the date the special event is scheduled to occur. However, no application shall be accepted earlier than one year prior to the date of the proposed special event.
(h) Permit fee. In addition to the application fee, the producer shall pay a permit fee in order to conduct a special event within the city. The amount of said fee shall be based on the services which the city may elect to provide to the producer of such special event and shall be equal to the estimated actual cost to the city to provide such services. The initial permit fee shall be the aggregate of the estimated costs of such services. If, at the conclusion of the special event, the cost of the services provided by the city is greater than the initial permit fee, the producer of the event shall be billed for the difference. Failure to pay the outstanding amount within 30 days of the billing date shall be a violation of this division. The initial permit fee shall be paid in full prior to the issuance of the special event permit for such special event. The application fee and the permit fee specified in this division shall be in addition to any other fees which may be required by any other ordinances or regulations of the city which might be applicable to such special event. No producer of any special event, except as otherwise provided for, shall be exempt from the payment of the appropriate fees required under this division, except as authorized by the mayor and city council.

1170:
(a) Definitions. For purposes of this section:
Camp or camping means to reside, lodge, or sleep temporarily outdoors, with or without bedding or other shelter materials, or to store personal belongings in a manner indicative of overnight occupancy, including but not limited to tents, tarps, sleeping bags, or other bedding.
Public property means any real property owned, leased, or controlled by the city, including but not limited to streets, sidewalks, alleys, parks, public parking lots, and other public rights-of-way.
(b) Prohibition.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to camp, lodge, sleep or store personal property on any public property within the City of Cleveland except as expressly authorized by the city.
(2) It shall be unlawful to camp, sleep, store personal property, sit on, or lie down on any public park, public street, or other public property so as to interfere with ingress or egress from such public park, public street, or other public property, or any combination thereof, or so as to interfere with ingress and egress to any private property accessed by means of such a public park, public street, or other public property, or any combination thereof.
(3) It shall be unlawful for anyone other than the owner of a private property, a leaseholder of such private property, or other lawful occupant of such private property to camp, sleep, reside, store personal property, or lie upon, any private property without the owner's or leaseholder's permission. Any such use of private property authorized by and consented to by the owner or leaseholder of such private property must be in conformity with the provisions of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Cleveland, including, but not limited to, the zoning and land use provisions of said Code of Ordinances which are applicable to such private property, and if such use is a violation of said Code of Ordinances, an authorization of such use by the landowner or leaseholder shall not nullify a violation of any provision of this section.
(4) It shall be unlawful to erect or maintain any structure, shelter, or bedding for the purpose of camping on public property without the express written permission of the city.
(5) No person shall store personal property, including but not limited to bedding, sleeping bags, clothing, tents, or cooking equipment, on public property in a manner that interferes with public use, access, or safety.
(c) Exceptions. This section shall not apply:
(1) When a person is authorized by permit, contract, or agreement with the City to camp in a specific location; or
(2) When enforcement of this ordinance would violate a person's constitutional rights under applicable federal or state law, including when no shelter space is reasonably available, pursuant to legal precedent.
(d) Enforcement and penalties.
(1) A violation of this ordinance constitutes a civil infraction and is subject to a fine of up to $500.00 per violation.
(2) Continued or repeated violations may be enforced as a misdemeanor offense, punishable by up to 90 days in jail and/or a fine of up to $1,000.00.
(3) The city may remove and store any unauthorized structures or items left on public property in violation of this ordinance, subject to procedures for notice and retrieval.
(Ord. No. 2013-06, 11-4-2013; Ord. No. 2025-02, §§ 1—4, 7-7-2025)

City means the City of Cleveland, Georgia.
Codified Ordinances and Code of Ordinances means those ordinances codified in the Code of Ordinances of the City of Cleveland, together with those ordinances duly ordained and adopted by the Mayor and Council of the City of Cleveland, but not yet codified.
Construct means, but shall not be limited to, dig, bore, tunnel, trench, excavate, obstruct, install or remove signs, or facilities, other than landscaping or ornamental plantings, in, on, above, within, over, below, under, or through any part of the rights-of-way. FCC means the Federal Communications Commission or any successor thereto.

This article shall be known as the "Telecommunications Antennae and Towers Standards Ordinance."

1251:
As used in this article, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
Administrator means the City Administrator of the City of Cleveland, or his or her designee.
Antenna means any exterior apparatus designed for the sending and/or receiving of electromagnetic waves for telephonic, radio, television, or personal wireless services. For the purposes of this article, the term "antenna" does not include:
(1) Any tower and antenna under 70 feet in total height which is owned and operated by an amateur radio operator licensed by the Federal Communications Commission;
(2) Any device designed for over-the-air reception of radio or television broadcast signals, multi-channel multi-point distribution service or direct broadcast satellite service; or
(3) Any cable television head end or hub towers and antennae used solely for cable television services.
Camouflage or stealth means techniques to disguise, hide, or conceal cell towers from view. Such techniques must include designs appropriate to the area of installation.
Governing body means the Mayor and Council of the City of Cleveland. For the purposes of this article, the words "city" and "governing body" are one and the same.
Micro telecommunications facilities are those which are located on existing buildings, poles or other existing support structures where antennae do not project more than 20 feet above the top of the structure and there are no more than six antennae per site.
Monopole tower means a telecommunications tower consisting of a single pole, constructed without guy wires or ground anchors.
Telecommunications facilities refers to antennae and towers, either individually or together.
Tower means a structure or facility, including but not limited to a lattice tower, guy tower, or monopole constructed as a free-standing structure, or in association with a building, other permanent structure or equipment, on which is located one or more antennae intended for transmitting or receiving of analog, digital, microwave, cellular, telephone, personal wireless service or similar forms of electronic communication. The term includes microwave towers, common carrier towers, and cellular telephone towers, and associated facilities, structures and antennas.
Whip antenna means a flexible, vertical rod, or radio antenna that would bend without breaking.
(Ord. No. 2011-21, § II, 12-12-2011)
1252:
This article shall apply to any telecommunications tower construction, erection, maintenance and/or renovation, and/or upgrade activity undertaken on any telecommunications tower in the corporate limits of the City of Cleveland by any person or persons, legal or natural, except for the following:
(1) Any tower and antenna under 70 feet in total height which is owned and operated by an amateur radio operator licensed by the Federal Communications Commission; provided, however, that the construction of any such and antenna is not located within 200 feet of any waterway.
(2) Any tower or antenna owned and/or operated by the City of Cleveland.
(Ord. No. 2011-21, § III, 12-12-2011)
1253:
The general requirements for telecommunications towers set forth in this section shall govern the location and construction of all telecommunications towers within the City of Cleveland, to-wit:
(1) Height. No telecommunications tower shall exceed 200 feet in total height.
(2) Building codes and safety standards. To ensure the structural integrity of telecommunications towers, the owner of a telecommunications tower shall ensure that it is constructed, operated, maintained and/or repaired in compliance with all applicable City of Cleveland codes, ordinances, rules and regulations. Owners of telecommunications facilities shall conduct periodic inspections of such facilities at least once every year to ensure structural integrity. Inspections shall be conducted by a qualified, independent engineer licensed to practice in Georgia. The results of such inspection shall be provided to the city administrator.
(3) Regulatory compliance.
a. All telecommunications facilities must meet or exceed current standards and regulations of the Federal Aviation Administration, the Federal Communications Commission and any other agency of the state or federal government with the authority to regulate telecommunications facilities and/or towers. If such standards and regulations are changed then the owners of the telecommunications facilities and/or towers governed by this article shall bring such telecommunications facilities and/or towers into compliance with such revised standards and regulations within the date established by the agency promulgating such standards or regulations.
b. Owners of telecommunications facilities shall provide documentation showing that each telecommunications facility and/or tower is in compliance with all applicable federal and state requirements. Evidence of compliance must be submitted to the City of Cleveland every 12 months.
(4) Security. All telecommunications facilities and/or towers shall be equipped with an appropriate anti-climbing device or other similar protective device to prevent unauthorized access to the telecommunications facility.
(5) Lighting. No illumination is permitted on telecommunications facilities and/or towers unless required by the Federal Communications Commission, Federal Aviation Administration, or other state or federal agency of competent jurisdiction, or unless necessary for air traffic safety. If lighting is required or necessary, the city shall review the available lighting alternatives and approve the design that would cause the least disturbance to the surrounding uses and views.
(6) Advertising. No advertising is permitted on telecommunications facilities and/or towers. However, a whip antenna may be allowed on any legally permitted permanent billboard or outdoor advertising sign as long as the other requirements of this article and the other codes, ordinances, rule and regulations of the City of Cleveland are met.
(7) Visual impact.
a. Telecommunications facilities and/or towers shall be camouflaged or stealth to an appropriate design for the area of installation, including, but not limited to, such telecommunications facilities and/or towers located on property owned, leased, or otherwise controlled by the City of Cleveland, regardless of whether or not such city property is located in the City of Cleveland or not. Design must be pre-approved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Cleveland. Telecommunication facilities and/or towers are subject to all applicable standards of the Federal Aviation Administration and other federal and state agencies.
b. If an antenna is installed on a structure other than a tower, the antenna and associated electrical and mechanical equipment must be of a neutral color that is identical to, or closely compatible with, the color of the supporting tower so as to make the antenna and related equipment as visually unobtrusive as possible. Roof-mounted antennas shall be made visually unobtrusive by screening to match existing air conditioning units, stairs, elevator towers or other background.
c. Where feasible, telecommunications facilities and/or towers should be placed directly above, below or incorporated within the vertical design elements of a the associated building or structure in order to help in camouflaging such facilities and towers.
d. Telecommunications facilities and/or towers shall not be placed in a direct line of sight with historic or scenic view corridors as designated by the governing body or by any state or federal law or agency.
e. Any equipment shelter or cabinet that is associated with telecommunications facilities and/or towers must be concealed from public view or made visually compatible with the architecture of the surrounding structures or placed underground. Equipment shelters or cabinets shall be screened from public view by using landscaping or materials and colors consistent with the surrounding visual backdrop. The shelter or cabinet must be regularly maintained.
(8) Landscaping.
a. To the extent reasonably possible landscaping shall be used to effectively screen the view of the telecommunications facility and/or tower from any public way, public property and/or public or private residential property.
b. Native vegetation on the telecommunications facility and/or tower site shall be preserved to the greatest practical extent and disturbance of the existing topography shall be minimized. The applicant shall provide a site plan showing existing significant vegetation to be removed and vegetation to be replanted to replace that lost.
c. The City of Cleveland may waive or modify the landscaping requirement where lesser requirements are desirable for adequate visibility for security purposes; for continued operation of existing bona fide agricultural or forest uses, such as farms, nurseries and tree farms; or where an antenna is placed on an existing structure. In certain approved locations where the visual impact of the tower would be minimal, such as remote agricultural locations or in developed industrial areas, the landscaping requirement may be modified or waived by the city.
(9) Maintenance impacts. Equipment at a transmission facility and/or tower shall be automated to the greatest extent possible in order to reduce traffic and congestion. Where the transmission facility and/or tower site abuts or has access to a public street or highway, access for maintenance vehicles shall be exclusively by means of such public street of highway.
(10) Principal, accessory and joint uses.
a. Accessory structures used in direct support of a telecommunications facility and/or tower shall be allowed, but may not be used for offices or vehicle storage. Mobile or immobile equipment not used in direct support of a telecommunications facility and/or tower shall not be stored or parked on the site of the telecommunications facility and/or tower.
b. Telecommunications facilities and/or towers may be located on sites containing another principal use if such site is otherwise in compliance with all applicable codes, ordinances, rule and regulations of the City of Cleveland.
(11) Lot size and setbacks.
a. All property necessary to satisfy setback requirements covering the total height of the tower shall be under the ownership or control of the applicant. The requirements for control may be satisfied by a properly executed and recorded (in the Deed Records of the Office of Clerk, Superior Court, White County, Georgia), instrument creating a perpetual easement.
b. Telecommunications towers must be set back from any adjacent property line, as measured radially from the base of the tower to said adjacent property line, a distance equal to the sum of the total height of the tower, plus the building set back distance specified for the tower site in the City of Cleveland Zoning Ordinance.
c. The following setback requirements shall apply to all telecommunications facilities and/or towers:
1. Telecommunications towers must be set back from any off-site residential structure, as measured radially from the base of the tower to said off-site residential structure, a distance equal to the sum of the total height of the tower, plus the building set back distance specified for the tower site in the City of Cleveland Zoning Ordinance.
2. Each and every guy wire and accessory facility must satisfy the minimum building setback requirements of this article and the City of Cleveland Zoning Ordinance as though such guy wire and/or accessory facility were a separate structure. The point at which each guy wire is attached to the ground (i.e., the "ground end") shall be subject to the same setback requirements as though said ground end point were an antenna, and, as measured radially from said ground point to said adjacent property line, a distance equal to the sum of the length of the guy wire, plus the building set back distance specified for the tower site in the City of Cleveland Zoning Ordinance.
3. For antennas attached to the roof of a supporting structure, or on a rooftop, a 1:1 setback ration (example: ten-foot high antenna and supporting structure requires ten-foot setback from edge of roof) shall be maintained unless an alternative placement is shown to reduce visual impact, and such alternate placement is approved by the city.
(12) Additional requirements for towers.
a. Tower site location and development shall preserve the preexisting character of the surrounding buildings and land as much as possible. Personal wireless telecommunication towers shall be integrated through location and design to blend in with existing characteristics of the site to the extent practical.
b. At a tower site the design of the buildings and related structures shall, to the extent possible, use materials, colors, textures, screening, and landscaping that will blend the tower and related facilities to the natural setting and built environment.
c. In no case shall a tower be located in the front yard, back yard or side yard of a residential lot, or upon property classified as residential under the City of Cleveland Zoning Ordinance.
d. Towers shall not be sited where they will negatively affect any historic or scenic view corridors, as designated by the governing body or any state or federal law or agency, or where such towers will create visual clutter.
e. Towers shall be enclosed by decay-resistant security fencing not less than six feet in height and shall be equipped with an appropriate anti-climbing devices or other similar protective devices designed to prevent tower access.
f. Placement of more than one tower on a lot owned by the applicant shall be permitted, provided that all applicable state, federal and City of Cleveland codes, ordinances, rules and regulations are complied with. No such tower such lot shall be located closer to an adjacent tower on such than the height of the taller tower.
(Ord. No. 2011-21, § IV, 12-12-2011)

1274:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Crosswalk means that portion of a roadway ordinarily included within the prolongation or connection of curb and property lines at intersections, or any portion of a roadway clearly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface.
Intersection means the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curblines, or if none, then of the lateral boundary lines, of two or more streets or highways which join one another at an angle, whether or not one such street or highway crosses the other.
Motor vehicle means every vehicle which is self-propelled.
Official traffic signals means all signals, not inconsistent with this chapter, placed or erected by authority of the mayor and city council, for the purpose of directing, warning or regulating traffic.
Official traffic signs means all signs, markings and devices, other than signals, not inconsistent with this chapter, placed or erected by authority of the mayor and city council for the purpose of guiding, directing, warning or regulating traffic.
Operator means any person who is in actual physical control of a vehicle.
Pedestrian means any person afoot or in a hand-wheeled vehicle.
Pneumatic tires means tires of rubber and fabric or similar elastic material inflated with air.
Police officer means any officer of the police department, or any officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic or to make arrests for violation of traffic regulations.
Private road or driveway means every road or driveway not open to the use of the public for the purpose of vehicular travel.
Residence district means any street length between street intersections where more than 50 percent of the frontage is in use for residence purposes, or where so designated as such by ordinance.
Right-of-way means the privilege of immediate use of the street or highway.
Roadway means that portion of a street or highway between the regularly established curblines, or that part improved and intended to be used for vehicular travel.
Safety zone means the area or space officially set apart within a roadway for the exclusive use of pedestrians, which is protected or is so marked or indicated by adequate signs as to be plainly visible at all times while so set apart.
Sidewalk means that portion of a street between the curbline and the adjacent property lines.
Slow or slowly, when used in this chapter or on any official traffic sign, means that the speed of a vehicle shall not exceed ten miles per hour and that the vehicle shall be under perfect control.
Solid tires means all tires of rubber and fabric or similar elastic material other than pneumatic tires.
Street or highway means every way or place of whatever nature open to the use of the public, as a matter of right, for purpose of vehicular travel.
Through street means any street so designated by ordinance whereon traffic has right-of-way over that on intersecting streets, except boulevards.
Traffic means pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances, either singly or together, while using any prescribed lane of travel.
Traffic control signal means any device using colored lights, sounds or words or any combination thereof, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, by which traffic is directed to stop and to proceed.
Traffic lane means those spaces in a roadway bounded by real or imaginary lines prescribed for pedestrians or vehicular use.
Trailer means any vehicle without motive power used for carrying property or passengers wholly on its structure and designed for being drawn by a self-propelled vehicle, except those running exclusively upon tracks.
Truck means every vehicle designed for transporting materials.
Vehicle means every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a public highway, except devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-801)
State Law reference— Similar definitions, O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1.

Any vehicle, except when passing another vehicle going in the same direction, shall at all times keep as near the righthand curb as possible and shall at all times be driven in a careful manner with due care for the safety and convenience of pedestrians and all other vehicles.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-812)
State Law reference— Driving on right side of roadway and exceptions, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-40.
1318:
It shall be unlawful for the owner, operator, driver, or chauffeur of any motor vehicle to drive or operate the same or permit the same to be driven or operated on the streets of the city, unless the person operating such motor vehicle has a valid and currently effective driver's license as required by the laws of the state.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-815)
State Law reference— Drivers' licenses, O.C.G.A. § 40-5-1 et seq.
1319:
No person who is less than 16 years of age shall drive any vehicle within the corporate limits of the city, except as otherwise authorized by law.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-816)
State Law reference— Drivers' licenses, O.C.G.A. § 40-5-1 et seq.
1320:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate on the streets of the city a vehicle for which a state license tag is required, unless such state license tag for the current year shall be so attached to the vehicle as to be visible and legible at all times.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-817)
State Law reference— Registration and licensing of motor vehicles, O.C.G.A. § 40-20-1.
1321:
A vehicle overtaking another vehicle going in the same direction shall first give an audible warning and then pass on the left side of the overtaken vehicle and not pull to the right until entirely clear of it. No vehicle shall pass another overtaken vehicle on top of a hill, or a curve, or while passing a street intersection.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-813)
State Law reference— Overtaking a vehicle on the left, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-42; overtaking a vehicle on the right, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-43.
1322:
No person shall board or alight from any vehicle, or ride or jump upon the vehicle without the consent of the driver, or have any part of the body protruding beyond the limits of the vehicle while the same is in operation.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-814)
1323:
It shall be unlawful for any person while in an intoxicated condition or under the influence of intoxicating liquor or narcotics to such an extent as to deprive him of full possession of his normal faculties to drive or operate any vehicle in the city.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-821)
State Law reference— Similar provisions, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391 et seq.
1324:
No vehicle shall be driven within any sidewalk area except at a permanent or temporary driveway.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-828)
State Law reference— Obstruction of sidewalks prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 16-11-43; stopping, standing, or parking on sidewalks prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-203.
1325:
No vehicle shall be backed unless such movement can be made with reasonable safety and without interfering with other traffic.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-829)
State Law reference— Similar provision, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-240.
1326:
The driver of a vehicle emerging from an alley, driveway or building shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to driving on to a sidewalk or on to the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-830)
State Law reference— Vehicle entering roadway, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-73; entering highway from private driveways, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-144.
1327:
All drivers of vehicles, particularly motor vehicles, in approaching work being done upon any part of any street, by either city employees or employees of public utility corporations, or by permission of the city, shall slow down their vehicles until, in passing such work or workmen, the rate of speed shall be within the limit prescribed by the modifying word "slow" as prescribed elsewhere in this chapter; provided, however, that such workmen or the foreman in charge of them shall place ahead of the work or workmen, in such a conspicuous location that it can be seen by the driver of the approaching vehicle, a sign to read as follows: "Men working—slow—city law"; the letters of such sign to be in accordance with the Standard National Code, and preferably to be made of reflector buttons, but if reflector buttons are not used, such signs shall be properly lighted at night.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-835)
State Law reference— Yielding right-of-way in highway construction zones and for maintenance vehicles, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-75.
1328:
No person shall operate a vehicle in the city recklessly or at a rate of speed greater than is reasonable and proper having regard to the width, traffic and use of the streets or so as to endanger the property, life, safety or convenience of any person or property. It shall also be unlawful to suddenly accelerate the speed of a vehicle either from a stationary position or while in motion; or to accelerate the vehicle in such a manner as to cause any portion of the vehicle to swerve or slide, in any manner; or to drive a vehicle in such a manner as to cause the tires of the vehicle to make a loud or squealing noise; or to accelerate a vehicle in such a manner as to cause any tire of the vehicle to make or leave a black mark upon the surface of the street. Exceeding the speed limits provided in this chapter shall be prima facie evidence that said vehicle was operated in a reckless manner.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-822; Ord. of 12-13-2004, exh. A(7-822))
State Law reference— Driver to use due care; proper use of radio or mobile telephone, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-241; intentional operation of motor vehicles to create danger to persons or property, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-251; reckless driving prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-390.
1329:
(a) It shall be unlawful for the driver of any vehicle to drive the same when such vehicle is so loaded, or when there are in the front seat thereof such number of persons, as to obstruct the view of the driver to the front or sides or to interfere with the operator's control over the driving mechanism of the vehicle.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any passenger in a vehicle to ride in such position as to interfere with either the driver's view ahead or to the rear, or to interfere with the driver's control over the driving mechanism of the vehicle.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-823; Ord. of 12-13-2004, exh. A(7-823))
State Law reference— Obstruction to driver's view of control of vehicle, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-242.
1330:
(a) Traffic ordinances apply to persons riding bicycles. Every person riding a bicycle upon a roadway shall be granted all the rights and shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to ride a bicycle, roller skate, rollerblade, ride a skateboard, ride a scooter, or any other similar devices on public sidewalks or in city maintained parks, within the city limits.
(c) No person shall park a bicycle upon any street or highway other than upon the roadway against the curb or upon the sidewalk in a rack to support the bicycle or against a building or at a curb, in such manner as to afford the least obstruction to pedestrians.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any person to roller skate, rollerblade, ride a skateboard, or any other similar device on any public street or highway within the city limits of the city. Persons riding a bicycle upon a roadway shall be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle.
(Ord. of 12-13-2004, exh. A(7-824))
State Law reference— Bicycles and play vehicles, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-290 et seq.; bicycles to obey traffic laws, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-291; authority to regulate persons on toy vehicles preserved, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-371(a)(18).
1331:
It shall be unlawful for more than one person to ride at the same time upon a bicycle or motorcycle, unless such vehicle is designed for the use of more than one person and equipped with a seat for each such person.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-820)
State Law reference— Authority to regulate persons on toy vehicles preserved, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-371(a)(18).
1332:
(a) All drivers of vehicles, motor-driven or otherwise, who observe any person in the act of crossing the street from one sidewalk to the other at intersecting streets, using a white cane or white cane with a red end or accompanied by a service dog, shall immediately bring such vehicles to a complete stop and permit such person to cross said street in safety.
(b) The protection granted in this section shall be given only to those pedestrians who are wholly or partially blind. It shall be unlawful for any person not wholly or partially blind to use a cane of the kind described in this section or service dog for the purpose of signaling or stopping vehicular traffic while crossing the street.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-825; Ord. of 12-13-2004, exh. A(7-825))
State Law reference— Blind pedestrian right-of-way, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-94.
1333:
It shall be within the power and discretion of the chief of police, upon notice from funeral directors, having in charge any funeral to occur at the residence of any person, of the time and place of such funeral, to detail police officers to direct the passing of such house by vehicles other than police or fire machines or ambulances, during the progress of the funeral.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-826; Ord. of 12-13-2004, exh. A(7-826))
State Law reference— Regulations regarding following too closely not applicable to funeral processions, O.C.G.A. § 40-6-49; disruption of funeral procession prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 16-11-34.2.
1334:
No vehicle shall tow more than one other vehicle, nor shall the connection between vehicles exceed 15 feet in length.
(Comp. Ords. 1970, § 7-833(e))
